title: Zero Dollars: 10 Things Locals Do for Free
description: Dongguan’s no-spend map runs through exhibition halls, neighborhood reading rooms, archaeology, ceramics and a campsite set aside for the public. Some stops require registration or observe weekly closures, but none of these activities requires admission or a purchase.

cards.title: See the city story for free
cards.subtitle: Dongguan Exhibition Center
cards.notes: The center’s official site says it is free to the public. Its displays trace Dongguan’s history and development through documents, reconstructed scenes and multimedia; check the current closure calendar before going.
cards.short_summary: Walk through a free civic exhibition about how Dongguan became the city it is today.

cards.title: Meet prehistoric Dongguan for free
cards.subtitle: Dongguan Haogang Site Museum
cards.notes: The Nancheng government says the museum has been open free of charge since 2007. Visitors can see the excavated shell-mound site alongside pottery, stone, bone and shell finds.
cards.short_summary: Look down into an archaeological site and examine objects left by Dongguan’s Neolithic residents.
cards.source_title: 东莞蚝岗遗址博物馆—东莞市南城街道

cards.title: Trace Yuan Chonghuan’s story for free
cards.subtitle: Dongguan Yuanchonghuan Memorial Park
cards.notes: The memorial park’s official site identifies it as a public cultural institution open to visitors free of charge. The grounds and displays focus on the Dongguan-born Ming commander; temporary capacity controls may still apply.
cards.short_summary: Use the memorial grounds and exhibition rooms as a free entry point into a consequential local life.
cards.source_title: 东莞市袁崇焕纪念园 首页

cards.title: Read ceramic surfaces for free
cards.subtitle: Dongguan Weimei Ceramics Museum
cards.notes: The Guangdong Museum’s institutional profile says Weimei has maintained free public admission. Its displays connect historic Chinese architectural ceramics with contemporary building-material specimens.
cards.short_summary: Follow the changing techniques and patterns of architectural ceramics without buying a ticket.
cards.source_title: 东莞市唯美陶瓷博物馆—广东省博物馆

cards.title: Browse Keyuan’s galleries for free
cards.subtitle: The no-ticket half of Keyuan Museum
cards.notes: The museum distinguishes its two areas: the historic garden buildings carry an ¥8 ticket, while the comprehensive exhibition area is open free all year. Stay with the latter for a genuinely zero-yuan visit.
cards.short_summary: See the museum’s comprehensive exhibitions free, while treating the ticketed historic garden as a separate visit.
cards.source_title: 可园古建筑门票收费—东莞市可园博物馆

cards.title: Settle in with a book for free
cards.subtitle: Dongguan Library Dongkeng Branch
cards.notes: Dongkeng’s government explicitly describes the three-floor branch as free to enter. It includes general and children’s collections, periodicals, local documents, reading seats and a 24-hour self-service library.
cards.short_summary: Claim a reading seat, browse the stacks or bring children to the picture-book area without an entry charge.
cards.source_title: 东莞图书馆东坑分馆—东坑镇人民政府

cards.entity_name: Dongguan Cultural Center Songshan Lake Branch
cards.title: Use the culture rooms for free
cards.subtitle: Dongguan Cultural Center Songshan Lake Branch
cards.notes: The branch’s published free-service list covers its public spaces and multifunction rooms for activities including calligraphy, photography, literature and intangible-cultural-heritage experiences. Individual scheduled programs may require advance registration.
cards.short_summary: Drop into a public cultural space where exhibitions, study and selected workshops carry no admission fee.
cards.source_title: 东莞市文化馆松山湖分馆免费开放服务项目公示

cards.title: Camp in a designated zone for free
cards.subtitle: Tongsha Ecological Park
cards.notes: Dongguan’s culture and tourism authority says four designated areas inside the park are provided for free public camping under park rules. Bring your own setup and confirm weather or fire restrictions before leaving home.
cards.short_summary: Pitch a personal tent in one of Tongsha’s four designated public camping areas without paying a site fee.
cards.source_title: 东莞市文化广电旅游体育局关于东莞市政协十四届二次会议第20230031号提案答复的函

cards.title: Watch the lotus ponds for free
cards.subtitle: Dongguan People’s Park
cards.notes: A Dongguan Agriculture and Rural Affairs Bureau feature explicitly presents the listed lotus-viewing locations as free and names People’s Park among them. Flowering is seasonal, generally centered on summer.
cards.short_summary: Circle an old central-city park and pause at its lotus ponds during the summer bloom.
cards.source_title: 免费开放！东莞这些地方藏着大片“荷花海”—东莞市农业农村局

cards.title: Circle the lotus pool for free
cards.subtitle: Humen Park
cards.notes: The city agriculture bureau’s free-access lotus guide specifically includes Humen Park and describes its pond framed by pavilions and covered walkways. Come for the public park circuit even when the flowers are out of season.
cards.short_summary: Take an unhurried lap around Humen Park’s lotus water, pavilions and covered paths without admission.
cards.source_title: 免费开放！东莞这些地方藏着大片“荷花海”—东莞市农业农村局
